title: Composition of place. Ignatius Loyola, make haste to help me!
html_source:
Advice from St Iggy on contemplation and spiritual betterment is firstly to find composition of place.(The line Appeared in Giacomo Joyce as Ignatius Loyola, make haste to help me).
From the man himself:

*It should be noted here that for contemplation or meditation about visible things, for example a contemplation on Christ our Lord (who is visible), the ‘composition’ will consist in seeing through the gaze of the imagination the material place where the object I want to contemplate is situated. By ‘material place’ I mean for example a temple or a mountain where Jesus Christ or our Lady is to be found—according to what I want to contemplate. Where the object is an invisible one, as is the case in the present meditation on sins, the composition will be to see with the gaze of the imagination, and to consider, that my soul is imprisoned in this……‘.

Note the reference to the visible : see Proteus line 1 : ‘'The ineluctable modality of the visible: at least that if no more, thought through my eyes’.
